pick.name: Dodo Payments
pick.what: India-founded MoR: global cards/wallets, UPI + RuPay mandates, subscriptions, usage billing, licence keys
pick.why: Onboards individuals (PAN + ID/selfie KYC, no company), cheapest established MoR rate in the field, collects INR via UPI/RuPay/Indian cards for Indian buyers; pays out in USD/GBP/EUR to your Indian bank (INR wallet discontinued; $50 minimum payout)
pick.free_limits: 4% + 40c base (US cards); +1.5% non-US cards/APMs; +0.5% subscriptions/usage; +3% PayPal or BNPL; India domestic 4% + 15c; $1/refund; $30/dispute; payouts: table says Free, FAQ says $5 if payout < $1,000; $50 minimum payout balance; payout currencies USD/GBP/EUR only (INR wallet discontinued)

alts.name: Polar
alts.why: Best DX + OSS; India payouts via Stripe Connect Express
alts.free_limits: Starter 5% + 50c (orgs from 2026-05-27); Pro $20/mo 3.8% + 40c; +1.5% non-US cards; payouts at Stripe cost: $2/mo active + 0.25% + $0.25 + 0.25-1% cross-border; $15/dispute; refunds don't return fees

alts.name: Paddle
alts.free_limits: 5% + 50c all-in; India not on unsupported-country list; payout balance currencies USD/EUR/GBP/AUD/CAD (no INR); UPI only one-time USD to Indian buyers; sole-trader eligibility not stated

candidates.name: Polar
candidates.verdict: Alt: best dev UX; check Stripe Connect 'individual' type for India

candidates.name: Paddle
candidates.verdict: Alt: strictest onboarding, best brand with enterprise buyers

candidates.name: Creem
candidates.verdict: 3.9% + 40c headline-cheapest; India payouts listed (7 USD or 1% fee); individual eligibility and INR checkout unconfirmed

candidates.name: Lemon Squeezy

decision: Dodo is the only MoR that is both India-native (UPI/RuPay mandates, USD/GBP/EUR payouts (INR wallet discontinued), individual KYC) and cheaper than Paddle/Polar on headline rate. Its weaknesses are youth and inconsistent fee pages, so keep Polar integrated as a fallback; move to Paddle if an enterprise procurement team insists on a long-established reseller.
note: Verified: Dodo's INR wallet is discontinued, so payouts are USD, GBP or EUR only, with a $50 minimum balance. Fees confirmed from Dodo's own pages: 4% + 15c for India domestic, +1.5% for international cards, +0.5% for subscriptions. The payout fee still conflicts on Dodo's own pages (free vs $5 under $1,000).
details: CONFLICT RESOLVED: Dodo India domestic = 4% + 15c (pricing table + FAQ 'India domestic transactions are 4% + 15 cents', fetched 2026-10-28). The '4% + Rs4' figure appears only on third-party pages (lifetimo, toolmage, Creem's review) and looks outdated. Payout-fee conflict remains (Free vs $5 under $1,000 vs Rs5 domestic per older docs). Indian card/UPI renewals settle ~48 h after renewal date; default mandate floor Rs15,000.

verify.note: Pricing page confirms 4% + 40c, +1.5% non-US, +0.5% subs/usage, +3% PayPal/BNPL, India domestic 4% + 15c (FAQ: 'India domestic transactions are 4% + 15 cents'), $1/refund, $30/dispute, and the payout conflict (table Free vs FAQ $5 if < $1,000). Dodo's docs FAQ also says: no registered business needed; Indian individuals need PAN; KYC is government ID + selfie via Persona; BUT 'Support for the INR native wallet has been discontinued'. Payout currencies are USD/GBP/EUR only, with a $50 minimum payout balance (cannot be lowered). The pick's why/decision/notes claiming an INR payout wallet are stale. Dodo also auto-applies GST for Indian merchants based on customer location (FAQ Q31), which matters for the GST slot.
